profile.campus: Marysville Innovation Park, 55 acres, two buildings
profile.address: 14684 Industrial Parkway, Marysville, Union County, OH 43040
profile.reading:
Amazon Web Services Marysville, known during planning as Project Cosmo, is a two-building data centre campus on 55 acres at 14684 Industrial Parkway in the Marysville Innovation Park, Union County, Ohio. AWS filed a rezoning application in October 2024, applied for the project in February 2025, and received a reinvestment area agreement from Marysville City Council on 10 March 2025. The company committed to investing $1 billion, with the two buildings totalling 500,000 square feet. Construction was slated to begin in August 2025 and to complete in 2027.

No IT capacity figure has been published for the campus, and the two numbers that are published should not be mistaken for one. The $1 billion is committed investment and the 500,000 square feet is floor area; neither indicates how much compute the site will carry. AWS does not publish per-facility power for its own buildings, and Union County has not required it to.

What Marysville did publish is the price. The reinvestment area agreement carries a thirty-year, 100 percent exemption from property tax on the assessed value of the data centres. Against that, AWS committed to $15 million a year for fifteen years to the Marysville Exempted Village School District and the city, plus other community support. A thirty-year full abatement against a fifteen-year payment is the shape of most data-centre agreements in the state, and the arithmetic of that trade is a matter of public record rather than of estimate.

The campus sits within a much larger central Ohio build-out. AWS has said it spent more than $10 billion on infrastructure in Ohio in the decade to 2025, and in 2023 stated plans for roughly $7.8 billion more by the end of the decade, of which about $3.5 billion was directed at a five-building campus in New Albany. Since then the company has announced a $2 billion campus at Sunbury and acquired 590 acres in Jefferson Township, Fayette County. Marysville is one site in that programme, not a standalone project, and its power will be drawn from the same constrained central Ohio grid that led AEP and Amazon to install 72.9 MW of fuel cells at the Scioto Darby campus in Hilliard, about twenty miles south.

This entry is built from the city council decision as reported and from AWS statements. It is not yet mapped in OpenStreetMap, which is why it carries a press identifier rather than a way identifier: the buildings were still under construction when this registry last harvested the map.

profile.research_note: [2026-09-05, Claude] Checked against all seven existing AWS rows in Union County before creating this one: every one of them is on Industrial Parkway, Warner Road or Weldon Road in Jerome Township at about 40.12 to 40.14 north, roughly ten miles southeast of 14684 Industrial Parkway at 40.2228, -83.3371. This is a separate site, not an update to a mapped building, and it is not yet in OpenStreetMap because construction began August 2025. Coordinates from Nominatim on the street address given in the reporting.
